# Synthetic AIF, OGG, and WMA fixtures

Generated locally with FFmpeg 9.0.1 on 2026-09-14. Every fixture contains only a
440 Hz sine wave generated by FFmpeg: two seconds, 48 kHz, stereo. There is no
third-party recording, artwork, or private metadata. These generated test assets
are dedicated to the public domain (CC0-1.0).

Run from the repository root, substituting each row's encoder options and name:

```sh
rtk ffmpeg -hide_banner -loglevel error -y -f lavfi \
  -i 'sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000:duration=2' -ac 2 \
  -map_metadata -1 -fflags +bitexact -flags:a +bitexact \
  <encoder options> hifimule-daemon/tests/fixtures/<name>
```

| Name | Encoder options | Production decoder evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| generated-pcm16.aif | `-c:a pcm_s16be` | 96,000 frames |
| generated-pcm24.aiff | `-c:a pcm_s24be` | 96,000 frames |
| generated-pcm32.aiff | `-c:a pcm_s32be` | 96,000 frames |
| generated-vorbis.ogg | `-c:a vorbis -strict experimental -b:a 96k` | 96,000 frames |
| generated-opus.oga | `-c:a libopus -b:a 96k -f ogg` | 96,000 frames |
| generated-wmav1.wma | `-c:a wmav1 -b:a 128k` | 94,208 frames |
| generated-wmav2.wma | `-c:a wmav2 -b:a 128k` | 94,208 frames |

The fixture-only Opus encoder uses libopus; production uses FFmpeg's native Opus
decoder and adds no external codec dependency. Bit-exact flags remove variable
muxer metadata; byte reproducibility also depends on encoder/library versions.
WMA encoding introduces delay/trimming: the decoder tests allow one 2,048-frame
codec block relative to the two-second source and verify exact resume subtraction.

Tests expand metadata beyond 8 MiB in temporary files (AIFF ANNO, Ogg comment
vendor string with rebuilt page checksums, ASF padding). These exercise the
production reader's eviction and resume behavior without large committed files.

WMA Pro and WMA Lossless decoders are enabled in the controlled runtime, but no
synthetic fixtures for these variants are available here. DRM-encrypted WMA is
outside scope. Local tests do not establish installed Windows/Linux/macOS playback.
